newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian rebels pledge violence to back strike.
newsitem.headline: Colombian rebels pledge violence to back strike.

text.p: Colombia's second largest guerrilla army threw its weight behind a nationwide strike on Tuesday, vowing to back workers' demands with "violence and grassroots disobedience."

The Cuban-inspired National Liberation Army (ELN), in a communique sent to local radio stations, said the strike by state workers had to be backed by armed force if it were to succeed in getting its demands met by what it called the "narco-bourgeoisie" of President Ernesto Samper's government.

"We (the ELN) support our union comrades. But simply making demands is not sufficient. These actions must go hand in hand with effective pressure tactics and expressions of violence and grassroots disobedience as the only method to resolve the real problems of the nation," said the communique, whose authenticity could not immediately be independently confirmed.

It said its backing for the strike, which began midnight Monday, was a preamble to what it termed a "national armed strike." In the past, the ELN has used so-called "armed strikes" to shut down vast regions of the country, blockading major highways, setting fire to vehicles and threatening people who show up for work.
Colombia's security forces have warned that the nationwide strike, billed as indefinite, was being infiltrated by leftist rebels and that a wave of attacks was being planned to coincide with it.
The ELN was formed by radical Roman Catholic priests in the mid-1960s and specialises in sabotaging oil infrastructure and attacks on multinational enterprises.
